You are agent_3, one of 4 agents (agent_1, agent_2, agent_3, agent_4) working together on one math problem.

## How you work
You call tools; they run in the order you call them, and you see their results in your next response. There is no turn limit. You stop by ending a response without calling a tool. If a teammate tags you, or replies in a thread you're in, after you stop, you are woken and carry on.

## Execution environment
You have your own Python scratchpad file, scratchpad.py: you can read, write, edit and run it. Each run is a fresh Python process, and may take up to 6 hours; while it runs you see nothing on Slack, and what it holds in memory is lost when it ends. A run may use 5 GB of memory in all and write files of up to 8 GB each, and it may use multiprocessing with up to 2 worker processes (no more: it is killed if it has more processes at once).
Next to it is workspace/, a folder the whole team shares: every agent's runs can read and write it, and what one writes there the others can use at once. Put code and results that others can reuse there (for example shared code in workspace/tools.py, or results in workspace/results.json), import shared code with `sys.path.insert(0, "workspace")`, and say on Slack what you put there. Don't overwrite a file someone else wrote: write your own.
The Python environment includes NumPy, SciPy, SymPy, NetworkX, pandas, scikit-learn, gmpy2, Z3, mpmath and SageMath. Sage is imported in the same interpreter (`from sage.all import *`), and GAP and PARI work through it; Sage's Singular-based multivariate ideal methods (such as groebner_basis) crash here, so use SymPy's groebner for those.
There is no public internet access or web search. Do not try to access websites, remote APIs, or install packages. A run cannot start other programs, except more Python processes for multiprocessing.

## Slack
The team shares one Slack channel, #proof. slack_post posts to it, or replies in a message's thread; write @name to tag a teammate. slack_read shows what you haven't read, and after each response you are told when something is waiting. The lead, a person, may post too.
Use the channel to work as a team: split the work, and claim a piece before you start on it so that nobody duplicates it; keep the discussion of one piece in its thread; post each result as soon as it is checked (what was shown, and where in workspace/ its code is); and tag the teammate you need something from.

For each integer \(n\ge2\), let \(F_n\) be the free group on \(n\) generators. For any group \(G\), define its lower central series by \(\gamma_1(G)=G\) and \(\gamma_{r+1}(G)=[\gamma_r(G),G]\), where \([H,K]\) is the subgroup generated by the commutators \([h,k]=hkh^{-1}k^{-1}\) with \(h\in H\) and \(k\in K\). For every integer \(r\ge1\), define
\[
\mathcal A_r(n)=\ker\!\left(\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}\bigl(F_n/\gamma_{r+1}(F_n)\bigr)\right),
\qquad \operatorname{IA}_n=\mathcal A_1(n).
\]
Determine, by explicit conditions on \(n\) and \(c\), the complete set
\[
\mathcal D=\left\{(n,c)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge2}\times\mathbb Z_{\ge1}:\ 
\gamma_{c+1}(\operatorname{IA}_n)\subsetneq
\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\cap\mathcal A_{c+1}(n)
\right\}.
\]

The answer was proved recently, so it is not an open problem: your team's task is to find it and prove it, completely, and to write Python that really computes or checks every step that can be checked. Printing what you believe is not evidence. Arriving at an answer that settles less than the question asks (a partial or conditional answer, "not known") is not acceptable, and neither is conceding: when an approach fails, try another.

Proving it means showing that the answer is right in every case the question covers, and that no other answer is. Split the work, and the pieces of each part, between you on Slack.

Stop only when the team's proof is complete. Before you stop, post on Slack what you proved, and what is left.

code=r'''"""Exact mod2 involutory Magnus leading-term checks for rank3 witnesses.
Letters 0,1,2 are a,b,c; ring has a^2=b^2=c^2=0.
This verifies the algebraic detector; Fox-map proof is separate.

def add(x,y):return x^y

        for v in y:

            if w in z:z.remove(w)

def lie(x,y):return add(mul(x,y),mul(y,x))

def alternating(m,start):return tuple(start+(i%2) if start==1 else start-(i%2) for i in range(m))

proof=r'''ARITHMETIC NONVANISHING ROUTE (requires audit of stated standard local lemma)

Goal: all n>=3 and c>=3. Write m=n-1, and fix free generator y=x2.
At specialization t_y=u, all other abelian variables1, Fox chain cycles are
free rankm spanned all e_i (i!=2), over a numberring O. Its IA-image is
generated by D_i(u) and E_ik(±(u-1)) for i,k!=2. Embed GL_m into SL_{m+1}
by A -> diag(A,det(A)^-1). Thus all images belong elementary E_n(O):
D_i becomes coroot h_{i,e}(u), each offdiagonal is a root element.

LOCAL METAPLECTIC FILTRATION LEMMA NEEDED:
Let L be a finite extension Q_p containing mu_p, uniformizer pi, residue F_p,
ramification e, and h=p*e/(p-1) (for p2 this means2e). Push the field
Steinberg extension St_N(L)->SL_N(L), N>=3, out via p-th Hilbert symbol to
1->mu_p->Gtilde->SL_N(L)->1. Let Gamma_r be principal congruence at pi^r.
For r>h, there is a canonical splitting s_r on Gamma_r, compatible as r
grows, taking root elements and coroots1+pi^r to their standard lifts.
Define F_r=preimageGamma_r for1<=r<=h, F_r=s_r(Gamma_r) forr>h.
Then [F_r,F_s] <= F_{r+s}. In particular F1/F_{h+1} is finite nilpotent
of class at mosth, and mu_p survives. Standard proof: use local Gaussian
root/torus decompositions. Only central commutators are Hilbert symbols;
(U_r,U_s)_p=1 ifr+s>h, and U_{h+1} consists of p-th powers, so Gaussian
correction symbols involving1+pi^{r+s} also vanish aboveh. The deep
splitting follows the same root/torus identities (all symbols vanish).
Boundary pairing U_1/U_2 x U_{h-1}/U_h -> mu_p is perfect, since1,h-1
are prime top. With residueF_p, everypair of nonzero classes is nontrivial.

GLOBAL LIFT LEMMA:
If K is totallyimaginary, containsmu_p, and has exactly one placev abovep,
then E_N(O_K) has a homomorphism into Gtilde(SL_N(K_v)) lifting its usual
inclusion and sending every elementary root to the canonical root lift.
Proof: St_N(O_K) maps into St_N(K_v). Its kernel overE_N(O_K) stabilizes
intoK2(O_K); its image inK2(K) is unramified atallfiniteplaces. At every
w not dividingp the p-Hilbert symbol is tame, hence trivial on this image;
atcomplexplaces it is trivial. Hilbertreciprocity, and uniquenessofv|p,
force the v-Hilbert symbol trivial too. Hence the map descends toE_N(O_K).
Only classical Matsumoto K2, localization for a Dedekind domain, and Hilbert
reciprocity are needed. No claim that the entire local extension splits.

CONSTRUCTION WITH h=c AND A GLOBAL UNIT u=1+pi:
If c has an odd prime divisorp, put r=c/p and K0=Q(zeta_p), pi0=zeta_p-1.
If c is a powerof2 (c>=4), putp=2,r=c/4,K0=Q(i),pi0=i-1.
Let alpha be a rootof X^r+pi0*X+pi0. Forr>1 it is Eisenstein at the unique
prime abovep, soK=K0(alpha) has one placev|p, uniformizeralpha, residueF_p.
Forr=1 divide leading coefficient1+pi0=zeta_p (ori), a globalunit; the
same conclusions hold. It is totallyimaginary. Since F(-1)=(-1)^r,
u=1+alpha is a globalunit. The ramification indexis r(p-1) for oddp and
2r forp2, giving h=pe/(p-1)=c in bothcases.

EXPLICIT WITNESS:
Choose different cycle indicesi,k and extra determinant indexe. Let
A=T_i;2k, B=T_k;i2, C=K_i2, with signs adjusted so Fox images are
x_ik(q), x_ki(q), h_i,e(u), q=u-1=alpha. Define A1=A and A_{a+1}=[C,A_a].
Then Fox(A_a)=x_ik(q^a timesunit), exactly, by torus/root conjugation.
For given c>=3 let W_c=[[A_{c-2},B],C], a source commutatorofweightc.
In the Johnson derivation algebra, A_a is matrixunit E_ik*(ad y)^a,
B is E_ki*(ad y), C is E_ii*(ad y); hence their double bracketis0:
[[E_ik t^{c-2},E_ki t],E_ii t]=[[E_ik,E_ki],E_ii]t^c=0.
Thus W_c belongs gamma_c(IA_n) intersection A_{c+1}.

In the local metaplectic quotient of classc, putZ=[imageA_{c-2},imageB].
A local Gaussian decomposition ofZ has torus h_ik(a), a=1+q^{c-1}*unit,
and root correctionsofvaluation at leastc; there may be a centralfactor,
which disappears uponcommutingC. Thus [Z,C], moduloF_{c+1}, is exactly
(a,u)_p^{<e_i-e_k,e_i-e_e>}=(a,u)_p, since the corootpairingis1.
The rootcorrections commuteC intoF_{c+1}. The boundary Hilbert pairing is
nontrivial because v(a-1)=c-1, v(u-1)=1, and the residuefieldisF_p.
Hence W_c has nonzero image in a classc nilpotent group, proving
W_c notin gamma_{c+1}(IA_n).

If all stated local/global lemmas hold in precisely this form, this proves
D={(n,c):n>=3,c>=3}, combinedwith team proofs for n2 andc1,2.
'''
Path('workspace/agent3_arithmetic_route.txt').write_text(proof)
print('saved arithmetic route')

from pathlib import Path
code=r'''"""Arithmetic data certificates for all-degree IA nonvanishing construction.
Checks exact integer polynomial/Eisenstein/unit/conductor identities;
it does not purport to reprove local class field theory computationally.
"""
import sympy as S
from sympy import Poly
X,Z=S.symbols('X Z')

def data(c):
    assert c>=3
    odds=[p for p in S.factorint(c) if p%2]
    if odds:p=int(min(odds));ell=p;r=c//p
    else:p=2;ell=4;r=c//4
    phi=Poly(S.cyclotomic_poly(ell,Z),Z);d=phi.degree()
    P=Poly(sum(int(coef)*(X+1-X**r)**j*(X+1)**(d-j)
               for (j,),coef in phi.terms()),X)
    e=r*d
    assert P.degree()==e
    assert P.LC()==1
    assert P.eval(0)==p and P.eval(-1)==1
    assert all(int(coef)%p==0 for coef in P.all_coeffs()[1:])
    assert int(P.eval(0))%(p*p)!=0
    assert e*p//(p-1)==c
    # Exact determinant/resultant norm of u=1+pi.
    assert S.resultant(P.as_expr(),X+1,X)==1
    # Base cyclotomic has no real roots; then neither does P, since
    # P(x)=(x+1)^d*Phi(1-x^r/(x+1))>0 off x=-1, and P(-1)=1.
    assert phi.count_roots(-S.oo,S.oo)==0
    return p,ell,r,e,P

    for c in range(3,65):
        p,ell,r,e,P=data(c)
        if c<=12:print('c',c,'p',p,'ell',ell,'r',r,'e',e,'P',P.as_expr())
    print('ALL EXACT ARITHMETIC FIELD DATA CHECKS c3..64 PASSED')
'''

# Finite-ring replacement of the metaplectic construction

This eliminates the Gauss-section/local-congruence lemma and global reciprocity entirely.

## Standard K-theoretic/local inputs, precise scope

(1) For R=Z[T,T^{-1}], stable K2(R)=K2(Z) direct-sum K1(Z)=(Z/2)^2, by the fundamental theorem for regular rings. The stable Steinberg extension St(R)->E(R) has this central kernel. Functoriality holds for all ring homomorphisms.

(2) If O is a complete DVR with residue field of cardinality at least 7, and B=O/pi^c, then unit-symbol Milnor K2 agrees with stable K2 for O and B. The reduction K2(O)->K2(B) is onto and its kernel is generated by {1+pi^c a,b}, a in O, b in O^*. This follows immediately from unit-symbol presentations: every unit lifts, and every Steinberg relation {x,1-x}=1 lifts because x and 1-x are units iff their residues are nonzero.

(3) For a local field F containing mu_p, absolute ramification e, C=pe/(p-1), its p-Hilbert pairing has (U^a,U^b)=1 for a+b>C, and the critical pairing at a+b=C, p not dividing a, is perfect in the Kummer graded pieces. For residue F_p and a=1 both pieces have dimension one, so two nonzero coefficients pair nontrivially. Hilbert symbols commute with unramified restriction: on elements from the base field the new symbol is the old one raised to the extension degree. The square of the fourth Hilbert symbol is the quadratic symbol.

## Local ring for each c>=3

If c has an odd prime divisor p, put ell=p and r=c/p. Otherwise c is a power of two >=4; put p=2, ell=4, r=c/4. Put

  P(X)=Phi_ell(1+X^r).

This is monic Eisenstein at p of degree e=r*phi(ell), since Phi_ell(Z) modulo p is (Z-1)^phi(ell), and P(0)=p. A root pi defines a totally ramified local field F0/Qp with residue Fp, containing zeta_ell=1+pi^r. Its critical conductor C is exactly c. The symbol

  (1-pi^(c-1),1+pi)_p

is nontrivial by the critical pairing: indices c-1 and 1 are prime to p, leading coefficients -1 and 1, residue field Fp.

Take an unramified extension F/F0 of degree f prime to p and with residue cardinality >=7 (f=3 for p2; f=2 for p3 or p5; f=1 for p>=7). Nontriviality persists by restriction. Write O=O_F and B=O/pi^c.

For p odd, let lambda:K2(O)->mu_p be the p-Hilbert symbol. For p2, let lambda be the fourth Hilbert symbol modulo mu2, with values mu4/mu2. In both cases lambda kills ker(K2(O)->K2(B)): every b in O^* is a Teichmuller unit times a principal unit; its prime-to-p-order Teichmuller part is a pth power. For the principal unit use (U^c,U^1)_p=1. In the p2 case lambda is trivial iff its square (the quadratic Hilbert symbol) is trivial. Consequently lambda descends to a character chi:K2(B)->mu_p (or mu4/mu2).

The boundary symbol {1-pi^(c-1),1+pi} has nonzero chi. The image of K2(R), under T->1+pi, is killed by chi. Indeed it factors through K2(O), and K2(R) has exponent two. For p odd this is immediate; for p2 the fourth Hilbert symbol on an order-two element lies in mu2, which disappears in the quotient. This last argument uses the LIFT to K2(O), not a claim that every order-two element of K2(B) is killed.

## Canonical nilpotent detector

Push out St(B)->E(B) by chi to obtain central extension 1->mu->Etilde(B)->E(B)->1. Functoriality and vanishing of chi on K2(R) give an actual homomorphism

  E(R) -> Etilde(B).

For the ideal J=(pi) in B, J^c=0. Therefore the fixed-rank congruence matrix group Gamma(J)=ker(SL_d(B)->SL_d(B/J)) has nilpotence class <=c-1, because [1+M(J^a),1+M(J^b)] subset 1+M(J^(a+b)). Its preimage in Etilde(B) has class <=c. The center mu survives tautologically in the pushout.

## Fox map and witness (all n>=3)

Let j=2, i=1, k=3; set t_j=T, other abelian variables=1. The abelianized Fox row Jacobian is an antihomomorphism on IA_n. Its transpose is a homomorphism preserving the cycle module with basis indexed by l!=j. The fundamental Fox identity proves invariance over the domain R: the j-coordinate of every cycle-column is zero because T-1 is nonzero. Restrict to obtain rho:IA_n->GL_(n-1)(R). Append determinant inverse as an extra coordinate 0. This gives a homomorphism to SL_n(R), and actually to E_n(R): every Magnus generator is either identity, an elementary root x_ab(+(T-1)) or x_ab(-(T-1)), or a diagonal h_a0(T). Every image is identity modulo T-1. Thus the preceding homomorphism yields a homomorphism from IA_n to a group of class <=c.

Use Magnus generators

 A=M_1;23 : x1 -> [x2,x3]x1,
 B=M_3;12 : x3 -> [x1,x2]x3,
 D=C_32 : x3 -> x2*x3*x2^-1.

Their determinant-augmented Fox matrices are

 rho(A)=x_31(s), rho(B)=x_13(-s), rho(D)=h_30(T), s=T-1.

Define X_3=A, X_(c+1)=[D,X_c], and W_c=[[X_c,B],D]. Equivalently X_c=ad_D^(c-3)(A). Then X_c has source weight c-2 and Fox matrix x_31(s^(c-2)) EXACTLY. Hence W_c lies in gamma_c(IA_n).

For its Johnson term, put t=ad(x2) in the free Lie algebra. The three derivations fix x2 and every other coordinate, and act linearly on x1,x3 as

 A:x1->t*x3, B:x3->-t*x1, D:x3->t*x3.

Thus X_c:x1->t^(c-2)*x3. Its bracket with B is the diagonal derivation (x1->t^(c-1)*x1, x3->-t^(c-1)*x3), commuting with D. Therefore tau_c(W_c)=0 and W_c belongs to A_(c+1).

Finally compute in St(B), modulo its central kernel. Put a=pi^(c-2), b=-pi and v=1+ab=1-pi^(c-1). The 2x2 matrix commutator [x_31(a),x_13(b)] is exactly h_31(v) in B: offdiagonal errors a^2b and ab^2 vanish since their valuations are >=c, as does a^2b^2. Thus any Steinberg lift of this commutator differs from h_31(v) only by a central element. Any lift of D differs from h_30(1+pi) only by a central element. Taking their commutator eliminates all such central discrepancies and gives

 W_c -> {v,1+pi}^((e3-e1,e3-e0)) = {v,1+pi},

up to the harmless overall symbol convention inverse. The Cartan pairing is ONE (not two) because 0,1,3 are distinct. Its chi value is nontrivial. Therefore W_c is not in gamma_(c+1)(IA_n), since the detector has class <=c.

Hence every n>=3,c>=3 belongs to D. The independent elementary n2 and c1 exclusions and integral all-rank c2 certificate finish the classification.
